subject: Post-call: Acme integration & request/response schema questions
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: Acme integration & request/response schema questions

Hi Alice / Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + next steps from our side and a few follow-up questions to help our eng team prep for the tech deep dive: 

Recap (what we heard):
- Primary workload: product search + conversational support over product docs (semantic retrieval -> reranker -> chat UI).
- Hosting: Acme runs on AWS (us-west-2), services behind private subnets.
- Compliance: SSO + vault for secrets; no public API keys stored in-app.
- SLA expectations: low-latency interactive responses for support UX, batched embeddings refresh nightly.

Follow-ups / asks for tech call (Dev will join):
1) SDK & auth: Which auth pattern do you prefer? Options: vault-managed API key, per-service JWT exchange, or mTLS to a private endpoint. Any constraints from SSO/infra?
2) Routing & model variants: Do you want regional routing (us-west vs us-east) or tiered routing for lower-cost models for background tasks?
3) Structured output / tool calling: The example we discussed uses a structured JSON schema for actions (extract->search->call); do you need Redwood's tool-calling primitives (tool manifests + deterministic response schema) or are you parsing open-text responses?
4) Embeddings & reranker: Volume estimate for nightly embedding jobs (docs/embeds/day) and whether you want on-the-fly re-ranking vs offline reranker scoring. Also whether you require persistent vector DB in your VPC or are you ok with our hosted vector service behind a private peering.
5) Request/response schema questions: For the chat vs completions decision, any strict requirements around tokenization (we treat inputs/stop as token-aware), max_tokens budget, stop sequences, and streaming behavior (partial tokens vs sentence-boundary chunks)?

Attachments: shared our SDK quickstart and integration guide — redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf (see attached).

Proposed next step: 60-minute tech call next week with Dev Patel (engineer) to walk through a sample integration and config. Can you do Wed 2/25 or Thu 2/26? Please reply with preferred time and answers to the bolded items above (auth preference, routing needs, embeddings volume) so we can prep targeted samples.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf (pdf, 1.2MB)

From: Alice Chen <alice@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: Acme integration & request/response schema questions

Hi Marissa — great recap, thanks. A few answers to help you prep: 

Auth / infra:
- We prefer vault-managed secrets; we rotate keys nightly and have strict scopes via AWS Secrets Manager. Ideally Redwood can support API keys pulled by an internal service (no embedded static keys in client).
- SSO: Ok to exchange via short-lived JWTs issued by our auth service if required for service-to-service calls.

Routing / variants:
- Region: us-west primary, but we may failover to us-east. We want simple routing by region + a fallback policy that uses a lower-cost model for non-interactive background tasks.

Structured output / tool calling:
- We'll use structured JSON for actions in the chat UI (we parse action objects). Tool-calling primitives sound helpful if they enforce schema and make parsing deterministic; please bring an example to the tech call.

Embeddings / reranker:
- Volume: ~120k docs, ~10k updates per night (delta updates). We prefer the vector DB inside our VPC for compliance.
- Reranker: prefer on-the-fly reranking at query time for freshness but want a fall-back offline ranking for heavy loads.

Request/response schema (quick notes):
- Tokenization: we have legacy tokenization assumptions (client-side substring offsets tied to tokens). Need guidance on aligning token offsets — how does Redwood expose tokenization APIs?
- max_tokens / stop: We want a safe default so UI never exceeds 2s latency; please recommend model/params that balance latency vs helpfulness. Also explain how stop sequences interact with streaming (do streams stop mid-token?).
- Streaming semantics: Partial tokens are fine for progressive UI renders; we need deterministic end-of-stream and support for server-sent events (SSE) or chunked HTTP.

We can do Wed 2/25 10:00am PT for the tech call. Please include Dev and any infra folks. I attached a quick architecture sketch: acme-system-arch.pdf.

Best,
Alice
Alice Chen
Lead Product Manager, Acme Corp
Attachment: acme-system-arch.pdf (pdf, 450KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 08:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Acme integration & request/response schema questions

Dev / Rachel — forwarding Alice's replies. Key asks for our tech call (Wed 2/25 10am PT):
- Prepare sample SDK auth flows: vault-managed API key pattern, and short-lived JWT exchange example.
- Bring an example of regional routing config and a fallback policy for lower-cost model variants.
- Structured output example: tool-manifest + sample chat response that returns an action object (we should show how enforcement/validation works).
- Tokenization helper: need a snippet to show tokenization API and how stop sequences map to tokens; also explain streaming stop semantics (mid-token vs post-token).
- Embeddings: recommended pipeline for nightly delta updates and example config for running vector DB in customer VPC.

Alice asked for streaming semantics and whether stop sequences can cut mid-token. My take: we should recommend that stop sequences are applied at the model output layer; streaming may send partial bytes but we should flush only on token boundaries if possible for deterministic offsets — Dev, correct/confirm on call.

Thanks — Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call: Acme integration & request/response schema questions

Short answers (I'll demo code on Wed):

1) Auth + SDK:
- Vault-managed API keys: we support short-lived API key rotation via an API that returns ephemeral keys scoped to a model/route — good fit for Acme. Example: backend service authenticates to Vault, requests ephemeral key from Redwood token-exchange endpoint, stores in memory only.
- JWT exchange: we support JWT bearer flows for private deployments; can validate with customer JWKS.

2) Routing + variants:
- We can configure routing rules: region-based (client region -> endpoint), cost-tier (background -> gpt-3.5-like cheaper) and a fallback chain. Config sample: route.rules = [{if: region=="us-west-2", target: endpoint-west}, {fallback: [endpoint-lowcost, endpoint-east]}].

3) Chat vs completions (schema differences):
- Chat: message-based input, recommended for multi-turn with system/user/assistant roles. Model returns structured content or function calls (tool calling). Use chat API when you need context weighting and role semantics.
- Completions: single prompt -> completion, better for one-shot tasks or when you want finer control of tokens and stop sequences.
- Tokenization: we expose a tokenize(text) helper that returns token offsets (UTF-8 byte offsets and token ids) so Acme can align legacy offsets to current tokenization. We'll include code sample.

4) max_tokens / stop / streaming:
- max_tokens: recommend 256 for UI interactive chat (lower latency), 1024+ for long-form generation. We'll surface model-specific token budgets and calculate estimated latency.
- stop sequences: enforced post-token; we stop when the decode produces a stop sequence token boundary. In streaming we stream tokens as they are decoded; stop detection occurs server-side and we send a final end event when stop encountered. That means no partial token truncation is sent, so offsets remain consistent.
- Streaming semantics: we support SSE and chunked-transfer. Each event contains token, token_id, and cumulative text. We can optionally emit sentence-boundary flushes if you prefer fewer events.

5) Embeddings / reranker:
- For nightly deltas: show a sample workflow (delta -> compute vectors -> upsert to vector DB). We support hosted vector DB with VPC peering or a customer-hosted DB; we'll bring infra diagrams.

I'll attach a small bundle with sample configs and a minimal code snippet for tokenization + streaming (dev-samples.zip) and prepare slides for Wed.

Dev
Senior Software Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: dev-samples.zip (zip, 120KB)
